title: /sail's SKILL.md calls the sweep before /chart, or a tooth reds

how: Add one tooth to skills/sail/proofs/test_sail_sweeps_the_tree_first.py (PROVES clause for this ticket): read skills/sail/SKILL.md, find the first line invoking `python3 -m skills.sail.sweep` and the line of the '## 0. Prior art for skill-text teeth: skills/challenge/proofs/test_challenge_wiring.py and skills/intent/proofs/test_intent_skill.py read SKILL.md the same way. Questions a Haiku-level builder would need, answered here: Which file? skills/sail/proofs/test_sail_sweeps_the_tree_first.py only. Which PROVES key? add '<this ticket id>': {'1': 'test_skill_md_sweeps_before_it_charts'} beside the 92e0 block. How to find the sweep line? first line containing 'python3 -m skills.sail.sweep'. How to find /chart? first line starting with '## 0. Chart it'. What does the tooth assert? a pure helper _sweep_order_problem(text) -> str|None returns None for the live SKILL.md, 'absent' when no sweep line, 'after /chart' when the sweep line index > the chart heading index, 'no /chart heading' when the heading is missing; the tooth asserts None on the live text and the two mutation strings on scratch-built mutations of it. Must the build touch SKILL.md or sweep.py? No. Is the proof hermetic? yes — reads SKILL.md via the proof's own _REPO_ROOT, mutations are in-memory strings.

decisions.text: D2: the proof is plain pytest functions with bare assert statements, run by the file's existing runner (if __name__ == '__main__': raise SystemExit(print_teeth_main(__file__)), already at the end of the file) — follow the five 92e0d158b1bc teeth in the same file. _sweep_order_problem is a module-level function placed after the _SKILL_MD/_SWEEP_CALL/_CHART_HEADING constants (lines 39-41 in 9154af40), uses those constants, imports nothing new; it iterates text.splitlines() with enumerate, takes the index of the first line containing _SWEEP_CALL and of the first line that startswith _CHART_HEADING, and returns 'absent' / 'no /chart heading' / 'after /chart' / None in that order of checks.

decisions.text: D4: the three constants ALREADY STAND in the proof file, committed by the red proof 9154af40 — _SKILL_MD = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / 'SKILL.md', _SWEEP_CALL = 'python3 -m skills.sail.sweep', _CHART_HEADING = '## 0. D5: if Akien's answer to the 8p question declines the proofs-only build, the hollow stays red and the ticket does not cross PROVED: it retreats PROVEME->BUILDME, and the decline is folded onto the ticket as a decision line before anything is rebuilt. If he approves, re-run the D3 command and PROVED crosses on its evidence.

D6: the D3 wait is not polled and not guessed. The first --seal run prints one line 'ASKED Akien -> open-<12hex> (cairn question list): once answered, re-run --seal' — copy that id, send it to the peer akiendelllinux_cc_0, and end the turn (no waiter, no loop). Akien's answer is detected by running cairn question show open-<12hex>: it prints the question's JSON, and it is answered exactly when that JSON carries "resolved": true and a non-empty "answer" (his verbatim words) with "answered_by" naming him. An approving answer → re-run the D3 command; the hollow itself re-reads the question (hollow.approval, hollow.py:731) and prints 'APPROVED skills/sail/proofs/test_sail_sweeps_the_tree_first.py -> open-<12hex>' — that printed line, not the builder's reading of his words, is what lands the evidence. If the re-run prints ASKED again (the hollow did not accept the answer as approval), treat it as a decline under D5.

D7: the implementation of _sweep_order_problem is exactly D2's: iterate text.splitlines() with enumerate; sweep_i = index of the first line containing _SWEEP_CALL, chart_i = index of the first line that startswith(_CHART_HEADING); if sweep_i is None return 'absent'; if chart_i is None return 'no /chart heading'; if sweep_i > chart_i return 'after /chart'; else return None. Checks run in that order; no other logic.

decisions.text: D19 (supersedes D8's 'to:' value and all of D13; F34): the peer is addressed by NAME, never by socket. A socket path names one session and is dead when that session ends. At send time the builder calls the ListAgents tool, takes the row whose name is exactly akiendelllinux_cc_0, and calls SendMessage with to: 'akiendelllinux_cc_0' (the bare name, as ListAgents prints it). If no listed row has that name, the builder sends nothing, tries no other address, and stops the voyage there; the stop is reported as a measured stop: 'no peer akiendelllinux_cc_0 listed by ListAgents at <time>'.

D20 (F34, as 4784351e4838 D16): D6, D8, D11 and D17 describe the session tooling the voyage runs in (SendMessage, ListAgents, the peer channel, ending the turn). They are not this ticket's build, and this ticket proves nothing about them. Their availability is the session's: if a tool cannot be loaded or a send fails, that refusal is brought back verbatim and the voyage stops; nothing is worked around.

D21 (F34): the wait on Akien's answer to the 8p question is INDEFINITE and has no timeout, no escalation and no default. A timeout on his gate would make the gate advisory. The ticket stays at PROVEME until the question carries his answer (D10); nothing crosses meanwhile.
